title: Fourier tail bound by noise sensitivity
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$. If $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, then the Fourier weight on levels strictly greater than $\lfloor\delta^{-1}\rfloor$ is at most three times the noise sensitivity at parameter $\delta$; here the Fourier weight is computed with uniform measure, and noise sensitivity is defined by $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=\bigl(1-\operatorname{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f)\bigr)/2$ using the Fourier noise operator.
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
If $y$ is obtained from $x$ by flipping each bit independently with probability $\delta$, write $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=\Pr[f(x)\ne f(y)]$; then
\[
 \sum_{|S|>\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor}\widehat f(S)^2
 \le3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f).
\]
